olivia (customer): Hi team — since ~2025-07-20T09:37:02Z our production workers are getting intermittent 502/504 from /v1/generate in ap-southeast-1. Roughly 3-4% of calls either return 502 or hang until a ~30s client timeout. Tenant=bluewave-payments, model=redwood-3-medium. Sample request ids: bw-7c1a, bw-7c1b. This started around 09:36:30Z and is impacting user sync jobs.

kevin (support): Sorry about the disruption @olivia — escalating to SRE and Runtime. Can you paste a sanitized curl and the exact timestamps you saw? Also are you using long contexts / prefix caching?

olivia (customer): repro (sanitized):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3-medium","input":"check payment status","max_tokens":80}'

We noticed the failures coincide with our batch worker spikes. Timestamps ~09:36:30Z - 09:41:00Z.

kevin (support): Thanks — pinging @mahima and @derek.

mahima (sre): Pulling gateway+runtime logs for ap-southeast-1 09:35-09:42. Seeing a cluster of upstream 502s from model-proxy citing \"upstream read timeout\". Correlates to runtime nodes handling bluewave-payments showing repeated kvcache GET errors and TCP read timeouts to redis-shard ap-s-3. Snippets: 

[09:36:33] model-proxy-4 ERROR upstream=runtime-9 502 req=bw-7c1a \"upstream read timeout\"
[09:36:34] runtime-9 WARN kvcache: redis op GET ctx:bluewave:acct:42 err=read tcp 10.4.1.22:6379->10.6.2.11:50132: read: connection timed out
[09:36:34] runtime-9 ERROR prefix_cache: op=FETCH key=ctx:bluewave:conv err=connection reset by peer

Metric snapshot: redis_p95 for ap-s-3 jumped from ~2ms to ~210ms; connection errors and timeouts spiked. No memcached usage for this tenant.

derek (eng-runtime): Runtime note: we synchronously fetch prefix/KV before starting generation. If redis blocks the worker thread, the request may time out upstream. Check for cache_circuit events and whether in-flight requests were blocked.

mahima (sre): Found circuit logs and blocked requests: 

[09:36:35] runtime-9 INFO cache_circuit: state=opening reason=latency_spike fail_count=9
[09:36:36] runtime-9 WARN cache_circuit: state=open duration_ms=20000
[09:36:36] runtime-9 ERROR request blocked id=bw-7c1b wait=23540ms on kvcache fetch

Also noticed redis pod redis-ap-s-3b reported repeated slow syscall warnings then restarted at 09:37:05 — readiness lagged by ~30s which explains the connection resets. Eviction logs show heavy key evictions around the same time (many ttl=0 evicted keys).

redis-bot: pod=redis-ap-s-3b event=OOMKilled reason=Evicted memory_pressure timestamp=1721386625

kevin (support): Any quick customer-visible mitigations we can apply to stop 502s while you fix Redis? Can we route that tenant to a pool that disables prefix cache?

derek (eng-runtime): We have a runtime pool that was launched for high-throughput tenants with `--disable-prefix-cache`. I can create a routing override for tenant `bluewave-payments` and roll it out as a canary (5% -> 50% -> 100%). This will avoid blocking on redis but will increase token use and median latency. Recommend canarying.

mahima (sre): I'll also scale the redis shard (replica +1), bump `maxclients` and switch eviction policy to `volatile-lru` to reduce churn. I will restart the flapping replica after ensuring AOF/RDB is healthy.

deploy-bot: deployment started: route/tenant-bluewave-payments->no-prefix-cache canary=5% by derek

derek (eng-runtime): Applied 5% canary. Monitoring the routed requests.

mahima (sre): After restart, redis_p95 trending back to ~3-5ms but readiness delays caused ~40s of retries during which some connections reset. Eviction logs indicate TTL-churn from a short-lived job that populates per-request contexts.

[09:37:05] redis-ap-s-3b WARN Evicted 11234 keys ttl=0 cause=memory_pressure

derek (eng-runtime): Canary traffic shows 0/502s on the bypassed requests. Increasing to 50%.

deploy-bot: deploy success: route/tenant-bluewave-payments->no-prefix-cache canary=50% by derek

mahima (sre): With the extra replica and tuned settings, latencies and errors are dropping. Recommend flipping to 100% no-prefix-cache temporarily while we implement durable runtime fixes.

derek (eng-runtime): Flipped to 100% no-prefix-cache for tenant `bluewave-payments`.

deploy-bot: deploy success: route/tenant-bluewave-payments->no-prefix-cache canary=100% by derek

kevin (support): @olivia can you confirm if the 502s/timeouts have stopped? We'll keep this routing and follow up with a timeline for a fix and a credit for the impacted window.

olivia (customer): Confirmed — errors dropped to near 0. Median latency up ~11% but acceptable. Thanks for the quick fix.

mahima (sre): Incident quick summary: root cause = redis shard ap-s-3 experienced memory-pressure evictions and a flapping replica causing elevated p95 latency and connection resets; contributing factor = synchronous prefix cache reads in runtime that block request workers. Mitigations = route tenant to no-prefix-cache pool, scaled redis replicas, adjusted eviction policy and `maxclients`, restarted flapping pod.

derek (eng-runtime): Action items (runtime): (1) implement non-blocking cache fallback (async fetch + stale-while-revalidate or early-return) to avoid blocking request threads, (2) per-tenant redis op latency dashboards and alerting (p95>30ms), (3) routing runbook & playbook to quickly move tenants to no-prefix-cache pools, (4) guardrails for jobs creating massive ephemeral keys (limit TTL churn). Will open PRs and schedule rollouts.

kevin (support): I'll prepare a customer-facing incident report and apply a credit for the impacted window 09:36:30Z-09:40:50Z. @mahima @derek please drop graphs and redis metrics into the ticket.

redis-bot: incident logged: incidents/1789002222 - redis-kvcache - severity=high
